Integrate $f'(x) = (3x - 1)^{-1/3}$ using the reverse chain rule:
$$f(x) = \int (3x - 1)^{-1/3}\,dx = \frac{(3x - 1)^{2/3}}{\frac{2}{3} \times 3} + c = \frac{1}{2}(3x - 1)^{2/3} + c$$

Substitute the coordinates of point $A(3, 1)$ to find the integration constant $c$:
$$1 = \frac{1}{2}(3(3) - 1)^{2/3} + c = \frac{1}{2}(8^{2/3}) + c = \frac{1}{2}(4) + c = 2 + c \implies c = -1$$
$$f(x) = \frac{1}{2}(3x - 1)^{2/3} - 1$$
